Automatic: regex pass/fail checks on git diffs, API usage logs for cost/tokens/turns, lint/typecheck/test runs; LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet, 5 rubrics). Manual: one blind reviewer checked the 16 PR pairs against the same criteria (within ±5% of automated) and judged merge-readiness

Criterion: weighted decision compliance (regex + human check), merge-readiness. Averages over 3 runs. -- Claude Code baseline (claude -p, 5-min timeout) + Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Opus 4.6 planning per p. 4/12): compliance 19/41 (46%); 2/8 tasks at 100%, 2/8 at 0%; 5 blocking violations; merge-ready 2/8; tests written 0; build pass lint/typecheck 100%, tests 0%; total cost $4.13, 3,902K tokens, 165 turns, ~5.1 min/task; cost per merge-ready task $2.07. Quality: does not work (misses decisions invisible in code); cost: partly (cheaper, but 6/8 need rework). Baseline. -- Claude Code + Brief (brief build, 30-min timeout) + Opus 4.6 planning / Sonnet 4.6 coding: compliance 39/41 (95%); 6/8 tasks at 100%, 0 at 0%; 0 blocking violations; merge-ready 8/8; 838 tests; build pass 100% all; total cost $5.28 (+28%), 3,867K tokens (-1%), 187 turns, ~15 min/task (+194%); cost per merge-ready task $0.66 (-68%). Quality: works; cost: works (per merge-ready task) / partly (higher total cost and time). Config C (external orchestrator) not reported

Project: one seeded repository (dcbench), 8 tasks designed by the authors with 15 seeded decisions. Configurations: Claude Code vs Claude Code + Brief. Baseline: Claude Code with codebase only, no spec. Held constant: models (Opus 4.6 planning, Sonnet 4.6 coding), identical prompts without hints, repository; differences: timeout (5 vs 30 min), workflow (spec + mid-build consultation) and context. Acceptance tests: regex pass/fail checks per decision, human blind review; no functional test suite for tasks. Repetitions: 3 independent runs per task and configuration (48 runs). Human intervention: none during runs stated

Claude Code + Brief better on compliance by 49 points (95% vs 46%), largest gap on decisions invisible in code (baseline 0-33%, Brief 100%); zero gap on code-visible tasks TASK-012/013. Merge-ready 8/8 vs 2/8. Total cost +28%, tokens -1%, duration ~3x; cost per merge-ready task -68%, per correct decision -36%. SD across runs ≤0.5 decision points per task; no significance tests

Distinguished the two configurations clearly; 3 runs with low SD. Limitations stated: benchmark designed by the authors to create a gap (best case for context augmentation), partially circular (scores the same decisions Brief retrieves), no stronger baselines (spec-only, context-only, manual criteria), one confounded comparison (context + spec workflow + consultation), single human reviewer, one repository and one model family

Proof-of-concept, directional evidence only; confound of context retrieval vs structured spec workflow not isolated; needs ablations (codebase + spec only, codebase + context only, manual acceptance criteria), multiple reviewers, more repositories, languages and model families; Brief-specific implementation

Vendor study (authors from Brief). Title and abstract '49%' are percentage points. Model use for the baseline unclear: p. 4 says Sonnet 4.6 handles all code generation with no spec, while p. 4/12 say Opus 4.6 drives planning 'in both configurations'. Timeouts differ (5 vs 30 min). Table 3 gives CC + Brief TASK-004 3/4 (75%) while Table 10 shows both decisions PASS, and p. 6 says the augmented configuration achieves 100% 'across the board' (Table 5) despite 5/6 and 3/4 in Table 3. Table 2 'Avg Merge-Ready' delta '+75%' is a difference in points (25% to 100%). Tables 2-4 jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt from text p. 5-6. LLM-as-judge rubric scores not reported. Benchmark repository, 16 PRs and harness released (github.com/brief-hq/dcbench). No pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript
